# Appeal of Denial — Knee Arthroscopy / Meniscus Surgery (CPT 29881)

**RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination**
**Member:** Cameron Brooks
**Member ID:** W412154328
**Reference Number:** POC-5EDC35C98D-81118
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-13
**Plan:** MVP Health Care (Commercial/ACA), Vermont

Governing policy: *MVP Health Care 2025 Annual Notices for Providers (NY)*, effective 03/2025 — https://www.mvphealthcare.com/-/media/project/mvp/healthcare/documents/legal/2025-annual-notices-providers-ny.pdf

---

Dear MVP Health Care Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my requested knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881), denied on 2026-08-13 under reference number POC-5EDC35C98D-81118. The denial states that my records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking MVP to reconsider this decision. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for my condition.

## Why I believe the denial does not match my records

MVP's own notice policy states: "It is the policy of MVP to provide coverage for medically necessary health care services provided to our Members." My records show sustained, well-documented conservative treatment that did not resolve my symptoms:

- I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy (24 visits, 2026-04-08 to 2026-07-15) focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- I took NSAIDs for 8 months without adequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-10, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- My MRI from 2026-07-02 shows a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking.
- I continue to experience locking and giving way in the knee, cannot squat or kneel, and am limited to level walking. My exam showed positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion.

This is not an absence of conservative care — it is a documented course of therapy, medication, and injection that has not resolved a structurally identified tear with mechanical symptoms. I am asking MVP to review this evidence against whatever specific conservative-care threshold was applied to my case.

MVP's notice also states: "MVP Medical Record Standards and Guidelines Well-documented electronic or paper medical records improve communication and promote coordination and continuity of care," and "Unresolved problems from previous office visits should be addressed and documented in subsequent visits." My records reflect exactly this kind of continuity: the locking and mechanical symptoms noted at the time of my MRI were an unresolved problem that was tracked through my physical therapy course, medication trial, and injection, and ultimately led to my surgeon's recommendation for surgery once conservative measures were exhausted.

## Request for the specific criteria applied to my case

MVP's notice states: "Utilization Management Criteria MVP uses the most current version of InterQual ® criteria as a guideline for its utilization management decisions for inpatient services and certain medical services." The denial notice does not tell me which specific InterQual subset, edition, or criteria language was used to conclude that my conservative care was inadequate. MVP's own notice confirms that this information is available to me: "MVP Members may request a copy of the criteria used to make a specific utilization management determination by contacting the MVP Customer Care Center at the number on the back of their MVP Member ID card."

I am formally requesting, in writing, the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination, along with any other clinical guideline relied upon. Under federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules, I understand I am entitled to receive this information free of charge, and I am asking that it be provided so that I can fully respond to the basis for this denial.

## What I am asking MVP to do

I am asking MVP to reverse this denial and approve coverage for the knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881) recommended by Dr. Duval, based on the conservative care history, imaging findings, and functional limitations documented in my record. I am also asking MVP to provide the specific InterQual criteria used in my determination as described above.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-09 (180 days from the date of the denial notice). I am submitting this appeal to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if that is not available to me, I will call the number on the back of my member ID card to confirm where member appeals are filed.

Please let me know if any additional information is needed from me or from Dr. Duval's office to complete this review.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

Cameron Brooks
Member ID: W412154328

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
